Replies.Text:
Drafted from the ideas in chat (Claude Fable 5.1). The defaults are written into the text as decisions; these are the ones I am least sure are yours, each with my recommendation. Resolve with no reply to take them all.

1. **The order of the money.** The plan sells the desktop license and run credits first (Step 4), the team image second, hosting last. The alternative is hosting first, which earns more per customer but needs User Management, billing and on-call before the first dollar. Recommendation: as written.
2. **The commercial reminder.** Pro is enforced Sublime style: never locked, a weekly reminder when unlicensed after thirty days. The alternative is a hard trial. Recommendation: as written; a hard trial on an MIT codebase is a fork waiting to happen.
3. **The name.** The plan keeps Consensus-AI publicly and makes a rename conditional on the trademark and handle check before the launch. The alternative is to pick a new name now, while nothing links here. Recommendation: do the check this week and decide then; if it fails, rename now.
4. **Managed runs at cost plus 30 percent.** The alternative is runs included in Pro up to a quota and nothing metered, which is simpler and has no cloud piece at all. Recommendation: start with the quota only, and add metering when the quota is being hit; I will change Step 4 to say so if you agree.
5. **The measures.** A thousand stars, a hundred public `.consensus` folders, a hundred Pro keys, five team licenses in six months. These are guesses to be argued with; say your own if you have them.
3. The Name. Add a disambiguation paragraph to the docs which clearly identifies and links to the other consensus as a defensive measure.

Anchor.Text: The paid line, the managed runs and the hosted tier

Applied.Outcome: Taken as recommended on all eight points (resolved with no reply). The tiers are the plans the server checks, Free, User, Host, Site and Enterprise, the License being the Clerk metadata the store writes; the Ed25519 key, src/License.js and the key by mail are gone. The commercial desktop ask stays, Sublime style, pointing at the User license through the Local sign-in. Prices as starting points: User 10 a month or 99 a year, Host 25 or 249 with User included, Site 8 a seat a month with five at least, the one-time price dropped. The store webhook lands in Consensus (POST /api/store/webhook, src/Store.js) on our own server. The free Public server counts nothing; the three-member trial is gone. Managed runs are Step 5, through a relay on the session token with License.Runs; the old Team step is accounted for line by line. Step 6 is a Public server run by us with Host included. Statements 3 to 5, the line under them, Before any charge item 1 and the Measures follow. The Clerk plan (Limits and prices) and Teams (The parts, The order) brought up by a manual edit each in the same turn.

Replies.Text:
Reconciling Steps 4 and 5 with the per-person license model (plan Clerk, The license, built as Clerk Step 5 on 2026-10-20; Claude Fable 5.1). Steps 4 and 5 were written when a license was a signed key read by a server and a team was a licensed image; the model since is that licenses belong to people, carried in their Consensus-AI sign-in, and a server is bound to nothing and counts nothing. User Management, Accounts and Roles, Multiuser and Clerk Steps 1 to 5 and 7 are Finished, so statement 4 is met and only Clerk Step 6 (the production instance) stands between the plan and the first sale. Eight points, each with my recommendation; resolve with no reply to take them all, and I apply them onto Steps 4 to 6 and the frame around them as one revision.

1. **One license, the person's.** Step 4's tiers are Free, Pro, Team and Enterprise, with Pro a desktop key and Team a licensed image. Under the model they become the plans the server already checks: **Free** (the Local server, no sign-in, any number of installations), **User** (an Owner or a Member on any Public server where they hold an account), **Host** (runs a Public server and is its Administrator; includes User), a **Site** license (a Consensus-AI organization carrying User for its members, with Seats and Clerk's membership cap, sold at a discount) and **Enterprise** by agreement. The Ed25519 key, `src/License.js`, the key sent by mail and the offline check go: the License is the `{ Plan, Until }` public metadata on the Clerk user or organization, written by the store's webhook and carried into every session token, which Clerk Step 5 already reads. Recommendation: take this; it is one mechanism in place of two, and it is the one that is built.

2. **The commercial desktop ask.** Statement 3 says money comes from commercial desktop use; the Clerk plan says the Local server is free with unlimited installations. Both can stand if the ask is Sublime style and points at the same license: a Local server, unsigned-in after thirty days of use, says in About and once a week on start that commercial use needs a User license, with the Sign in button (Clerk Step 5 built the Local sign-in) and the pricing page; it never locks and never counts; a session holding User or above silences it. No key, no module of its own. The alternative is to make Local free for every use, commercial included, and strike the clause from statement 3. Recommendation: keep the ask, retargeted to the User license; on an MIT codebase it is a request, not a gate, and the User license is what the solo professional buys anyway.

3. **The prices**, as starting points in US dollars to test against the first hundred users, as before: User 10 a month or 99 a year; Host 25 a month or 249 a year, User included; a Site license at 8 a seat a month, five seats minimum, the hoster's Host license bought beside it; Enterprise by agreement. The one-time Pro price goes: the license carries Until, and a perpetual license cannot carry the run quota of point 6. Recommendation: these numbers, written as a table in place of the present one.

4. **The store and the webhook.** Lemon Squeezy or Paddle still, for the tax. The webhook lands in Consensus itself, not in a second codebase: a route `POST /api/store/webhook` in a module `src/Store.js`, verified by the store's signature, alive only on a server whose settings hold a `Store` section and the Clerk secret key, which is our own server (the docs host or the hosted tier's), never a customer's. On a sale it finds the Clerk user by the buyer's email, or creates one so the invitation mail is Clerk's, and writes License { Plan, Until } through the Backend API; for a Site license it creates the organization with Seats and the membership cap, writes the License on it and makes the buyer its admin; a renewal moves Until, a cancellation leaves Until to run out. The buyer then signs in with the same email anywhere. Recommendation: so; the Clerk section with the secret key for our own servers already exists for exactly this.

5. **The free Public server.** Step 5's three-member trial counted in the role folders goes. The image is free to download and run, holds any number of accounts and counts nothing; what a free team is short of is licenses, since the Administrator needs Host and every Owner and Member a User license, while Watchers are free. That is how Clerk Step 5 is built, so this is a statement, not a change. Recommendation: so.

6. **Managed runs move to Step 5, with a relay.** Runs on a Consensus key cannot be counted by the customer's server alone: our provider key cannot live in a desktop, so a run on our key goes through a relay of ours, which is the cloud piece Step 4 said it had none of. So: Step 5 becomes **Managed runs**: an LLM connection kind `Consensus-AI` in the Settings popup, pointed at our relay, whose credential is the person's session token (a Local server signs in for it, as for going Public); the relay reads the claim's monthly quota (`License.Runs`, written by the store with the plan: so many runs a month on User, more on Host, pooled on a Site), counts runs on our side and refuses over the quota with a plain answer the toast shows; bring-your-own-key runs stay free and unlimited; metering by tokens stays a step of its own, when the quota is being hit. The present Step 5 (Team) collapses into points 1 and 5: its Git sync is built in Work's options, its audit log is the activity history, backups are the export, and SSO (Clerk's enterprise connections) and on-premises terms are Enterprise's by agreement. Recommendation: so.

7. **Step 6, Hosted,** reads as a Public server run by us per customer: the Host license is part of the hosted price and the customer's team signs in on its own User licenses or a Site's seats; the rest of the step stands. Recommendation: so.

8. **The frame.** Statement 3 names the User, Host and Site licenses and managed runs in place of the desktop license and the team image; statement 4 says the server knows who is calling since Clerk Step 5; statement 5 orders the money as the licenses, managed runs, hosting; the line under the statements says Steps 1 to 3 start now, Step 4 waits on Clerk Step 6 alone, Steps 5 and 6 follow; Before any charge item 1 becomes Clerk Step 6 (the production instance, the token template, the License metadata) in place of User Management; the Measures count User licenses and Site licenses in place of Pro keys and team licenses. In the same turn two pointers are brought up by a small PUT: the Clerk plan's Limits and prices paragraph (which says these steps get a thread of their own) and Teams' The parts and The order (which still put Promotion Step 4 before User Management Step 3). Recommendation: so, with this revision.
